findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

On arrival the PIC was unable to provide a vomit/diarrheal event clean up kit or procedures. They normally have a body fluid kit sufficient for this issue available but were unable to find/produce it during this inspection. A procedure was given during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that the procedures/kit is available at al times in the facility.

findings.comment:
Raw shell eggs observed stored above lettuce in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Cooler rearranged to prevent cross contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Salads in the cookline prep cooler (bottom) observed at 75F. Technicians responded during inspection and got the cooler temperature dropping, but complete repairs will be completed by next Friday. Salads were moved to the functioning cooler to rapidly cool to 41F or below. 
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Thermometers in the vertical dressing cooler and the vertical cookline freezer observed to be damaged. Ensure functional thermometers are present in all cold holding units.
4-204.112: (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. [C]

findings.comment:

[Pf]

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
Chicken nuggets observed held without indicating the time they were prepared or when they would be discarded. Discussion with PIC indicated that they are held using time as a control. CORRECTED— Nuggets were still hot and allowed to be kept. Facility uses timers to keep track of discard times and the appropriate timer was set for the Wendy’s-established time for chicken nuggets (30 minutes).
3-501.19: (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. [P]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Employees observed using cups to scoop ice at the drive thru. CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC. Ensure staff use ice scoop rather than cups to scoop ice.

(D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: No sanitizer bucket present at time of inspection. Employee filled sanitizer buckets to appropriate concentration. CORRECTED— PIC and another employee adjusted dispenser. Sanitizer registered at 200ppm quat.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employee enter kitchen with gloves on and begin working. CORRECTED— Provided education. Employee returned to handwashing sink, removed gloves and washed hands before returning to work.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No soap provided at front handwashing sink. CORRECTED— Soap dispenser was refilled. Ensure soap is always provided at handwashing sinks.
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [Pf]

findings.comment:

4-501.114: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration of 200-400 ppm or as specified by the manufacturer's label. [Pf]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled

Knife observed stored in the gap between a knife rack and the wall. CORRECTED— Knife removed to be washed, rinsed and sanitized prior to storage in a clean location.
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips

findings.comment: PIC was unaware of any written clean up policy for vomit/diarrhea. CORRECTED-- Inspector provided a written policy. Keep available in case clean up is needed. Ref.2-501.11  [Pf]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Facility is not under the supervision of a certified food protection manager. Ensure sufficient staff are certified food managers to cover all shifts of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
PIC could not provide a written vomit/diarrhea clean up policy to be reviewed during inspection. A written policy (or a kit) must be available at all times for reference if/when needed.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

4-501.114: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration of 200-400 ppm or as specified by the manufacturer's label. [Pf]

findings.comment:
Drive-thru ice bin left exposed/open when not in use. Keep ice bin covered when not in use to protect ice from contamination. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC. Ice bin closed.
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. [C]

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment: Observed employee refilling bacon container on prep line with bare hands. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and provided education. Bacon will be discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11 (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in ¶¶ (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. (P)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed no concentration quat sanitizer in buckets and at 3 compartment sink (from dispenser). CORRECTED- PIC was able to adjust dispenser to dispense at the proper concentration. Dishes need to be re-sanitized and buckets need to be refilled.
4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. (P)

findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. (Pf)

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 (B) (1) (C) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Cloths used for wping counters in the kitchen area were observed stored in solutions of Quat the triggered a small color change on the inspectors test strips (approximately 50 ppm). Quat sanitizers should be between 200-400 ppm. The PIC adjusted the machine and new buckets were made at 400 ppm Quat.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 (Pf) A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

When asked, the facility could only provide test strips intended for chlorine (CL) based sanitizers. The sanitizers in the facility use a Quat based sanitizer. DIscussed with the PIC and instructed to aquire test strips intended for Quat sanitizers.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 (C) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

The mop sink in the rear of the kitchen area was observed with a side that was heavily chipped. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to repair or replace prior to the nextt routine inspection.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Bag of buns was observed sitting on top of clean, prepped lettuce at the make line. Bag of buns was moved off the lettuce by inspector. Management was advised to be mindful the general surface of packaging is not considered a clean surface. Make sure packaging is not in direct contact with prepared foods.

Employee was observed spraying disinfectant on general surfaces around chili hot holding and cup storage at the front counter. There was potential for the chemical to get directly on surfaces of single service cups where customers may place their mouths. Employee was advised to be careful when spraying the chemical to avoid getting it on the cups or in the chili (covered with a lid at the time). Employee sprayed the disinfectant directly on the cloth being used to finish wiping down the area.

Food and equipment shall be protected from potential cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a - Bolts on the sensor hanging down in the ice machine were rusty. Replace the rusty bolts.
Also, a small amount of mold was observed on the ceiling of the machine where the sensor attaches. Clean and sanitize in the ice machine as needed to eliminate buildup of mold.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Damp wiping cloth was observed on trays next to the front handsink. It appeared someone was in the process of wiping down trays and then left without completing the task. Manager noted the practice is to use one disposable wiping cloth for a set of trays and then discard when finished. Trays are wiped down with disinfectant or sanitizer spray. Manager was advised staff should discard the disposable cloth if interrupted during the process and then start with a fresh cloth when they return to the task rather than leave it sitting out for later use. Towel was eventually discarded.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.
Immediately dispose of used wiping cloths when they are no longer needed or an interruption occurs that would result in the damp cloth sitting out for an extended period of time when being used with a spray bottle of sanitizer.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - Moisture and what appeared to be mold was observed in the cabinet beneath the tea dispensers in the lobby. Clean in the cabinet.
Bottom inside the reach-in freezer at the end of the cook line had food crumbs in the bottom. Clean inside the freezer.

Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1280 - A jacket was observed hanging on the dry storage shelves by the back door. Store personal belongings in a designated area away from all food and products that are used at the facility.

An adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage areas to reduce the potential for cross contamination.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.citation_text:
750.540 - A certified food manager (CFM) was not on duty upon arrival of the inspector. Manger on duty stated her certification recently expired; manager will be taking a certification course early next year. Manger on duty stated the GM was in for a couple hours earlier that day. One of the other managers that has a current food manager certification started his shift at 4p. 

Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of CFMs to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  CFMs. 
Ensure that all persons who have the potential to be in charge at the time of inspection have a food manager certification.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: No FSSMC in facility. Rearrange schedule for FSSMC to be provided during all hours. 4 FSSMCs currently employed.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment: No hot water in facility.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment: Facility without hot water. Repair or Replace water heater.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed an employee using his cell phone, then continue straight in to prepping food. Employee was stopped, educated on washing hands, and asked to wash his hands prior to resuming food prep. Ensure that once hands are contaminated that they are washed prior to resuming work. 
750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the walk-in bun freezer to have an excessive accumulation of ice. Ensure that the ice is broken away to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface. The walk-in bun freezer should also be inspected for leaking from condensation line and door seals to mitigate moisture going into the unit. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment:
Facility did not have hot, running water during the inspection. Facility had hot water heater repaired yesterday. The hot water did return during the inspection, but for less than 30 seconds. The water then ran cold again. Ensure that the water heater issue is repaired to provide hot water throughout the facility. 
750-1120 Each lavatory shall be provided with hot and cold water tempered by means of a mixing valve or combination faucet.
750-1030 Water under pressure at the required temperature shall be provided to all fixtures and equipment that use water.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Observed the facility to conducting food prep with no FSSMC on site. Facility should have an FSSMC on site at all times during food prep and service. Facility employs 4 FSSMCs. The critical will not be left open due to this, unless the issue continues in the future. 
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed personal items being stored on the food surface of filters that will be used to filter the grease at the end of service. This poses a potential to cross contaminate the filters that will have the oil flow through them. Ensure that personal items are stored in a designated personal area that is below and away from food/food surfaces. Filters moved during the inspection. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the soda nozzles at the dispenser closest to the drive-thru to be soiled with an accumulation of debris. Ensure that food surfaces are regularly cleaned to prevent cross contamination. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed the self-closer on the back door to be in an inoperable condition. This has been the 3rd observance of this critical violation in the past year. Ensure that the self-closer is reattached to the door and remains intact.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the area below one of the self-service counters, in between the two self-service soda machines, to be excessively soiled with food debris. 2) Observed the back door's locking mechanism to be taken apart and in general disrepair. Ensure that walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures are maintained in good repair, as well as in a clean state. 
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.
750-1210e  Equipment attached to walls and ceilings shall be easily cleanable and shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Facility was unable to produce any FSSMC certificates during the inspection. Ensure that these certificates are readily available and that there is at least 1 full-time employee on staff with this certificate. 
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed raw bacon being stored above coffee in the walk-in cooler. Ensure that raw product is stored above RTE foods. Bacon and coffee moved during the inspection. 
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
1) Observed an employee wash their hands, then turn off the water without a barrier. Employee was stopped, educated, and instructed to rewash their hands. Ensure that a barrier is utilized when turning off the faucet to prevent recontaminating hands. 2) Observed an employee switching between the cash register and food handling without washing their hands. Manager was made aware and that the employee should be washing their hands when switching tasks. 
750-510d To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.
750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the inside of the microwave to be falling in on itself, which is causing a fan to be exposed. Ensure that the non-food contact surfaces are maintained in good repair, as well as in a clean state. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the ice machine baffles to have an accumulation of mold. Ensure that the baffles are cleaned at regular intervals to prevent cross contamination. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service articles being stored with the food contact surface side up without any form of protection over them. These articles were inverted during the inspection by the manager. Ensure that single service articles are stored in a manner that prevents cross contamination and handling of the food contact surfaces. 
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Observed no FSSMC within the facility during the inspection and the facility could not provide any FSSMC certificates. 
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed frosty mix in the frosty machine without a lid. After speaking with the GM, it was noted the mix had been in the machine for 2 hours at the time of the inspection. The frosty machine is just below head level for most people and poses a risk for cross contamination when not properly covered. The lid was found during the inspection and placed on the frosty machine. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the dust pans by the mop sink to have an excessive accumulation of damp food debris. The facility is having some issues with flies in the facility at this time, so these dust pans will not help the issue. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are properly cleaned at regular intervals. This is will assist in decreasing any pest issues within the facility. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment:
Observed the hand sink, by the ice machine, to not have adequate pressure for the hot and cold water. GM stated the hand sink had been in this state for a little while (no time specified). Maintenance was in the building during the inspection and cleaned out sediment within the pipes. The sink was running at proper pressures by the end of the inspection. Ensure that if a sink is not running at proper temperatures/pressures that it is fixed promptly. 
750-1030 Water under pressure at the required temperature shall be provided to all fixtures and equipment that use water.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed the back door self-closer to be disconnected. This is a reoccurring violation. Spoke with the district manager about the issue and he believes it is arising from the night delivery drivers. Maintenance placed the self-closer back on the door during the inspection. Ensure that the outer openings are properly sealed and provided with self-closers at all times. 
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed cut tomatoes on the cook line by the ice machine that were without a time mark and were at 47F probed. The manager stated they had been placed on the line at 11:00 AM. There is no time/temperature log and it is unknown as to when the tomatoes fell out of temperature. The tomatoes were discarded during the inspection. The cook line at this facility is consistently warm and the items in the cook line prep coolers tend to run at higher temperatures. The facility should time mark items when they are placed on the cook line and use them within 4 hours, or start a time/temperature log to identify when products fall out of temperature. 
750-153(a) When using time as a control. Food shall be marked to indicate the time when  it was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Properly label food.
750-153(a) Food shall not be held more that 4 hours past the point it is removed from temperature control. Do not hold food in excess of four hours after removal from temperature control.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed lettuce being stored in a container, in the walk-in, without a covering over the top. Ensure that when food is stored in a container that is provided with some type of cover to prevent potentials for cross-contamation.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed a measuring cup for strawberry syrup being stored in a single service cup with water in it. The employee stated it was used to clean the utensil in between uses. Staff was advised that this is a poor practice and should be ceased. Manager was educated on proper ways to store in-use utensils. 
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed an employee wash their hands, then turn off the faucet with their bare hand. Employee was stopped and educated during the inspection. Ensure that after washing hands the faucet is turned off with a barrier to avoid re-contamination. Employee rewashed their hands at this time. 
750-510d To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
Observed a personal drink on a rack sitting above food. Ensure that there are adequate designated areas for employee's personal belongings/drinks. Personal items should be stored below and away from food and products used with food. Manager discarded the drink. 
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed all the sanitizer buckets on the cook lines not to be at the proper concentration of quat (100 ppm). Ensure that sanitizer buckets are changed regularly and tested before being placed out for service. Employee made new sanitizer bucket during the inspection. 
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment:
While testing the sanitizer water it was noted that the water was consistently cold coming out of the three compartment sink. Upon further investigation, an employee regularly turns off the breaker to the in-line water heater that supplies the entire facility. This is a bad practice and should be ceased immediately. The facility should have an adequate supply of hot, running water at all times. 
750-820 For manual washing, rinsing and sanitizing utensils and equipment, each compartment of the sink shall be supplied with hot and cold potable running water.
750-1030 Water under pressure at the required temperature shall be provided to all fixtures and equipment that use water.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment:
Observed a mop bucket with dirty water in it, in the rear of the facility, that had a murky appearance with no bubbles noted. Dirty mop water is considered waste water and it should be emptied at the end of each use. Mop water emptied during the inspection.  
750-1050 All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
1) Observed the cold water handle at the 3 compartment sink to have a leak when turned off. 2) Observed the hand sink at the front of the kitchen to have a leak from around the faucet. Ensure that plumbing is kept in good repair and that any plumbing repairs is done by a licensed plumber. 
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed the back door to have light coming in around the top of the door and the self-closer to be in disrepair. The business was using a bungie cord to hold the door shut. This is not a proper practice. Outer openings should be tight fitting and have a working self-closer. Repair or replace the door. 
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the drain under the soda fountains, in the dining room, to be soiled. Ensure that floors and drains are maintained in good repair, as well as in a clean state.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the 3 compartment sink to have caulking that was both moldy and in disrepair. With the degradation that was noted to the caulking, it is recommended that the caulking be removed and redone. Ensure that walls, ceilings, and attached equipment is maintained smooth, easily cleanable, as well as in a clean state. 
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide 
properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed a bottle of Windex being stored on a rack that had food stored below it. Employee immediately moved the bottle. Ensure that chemicals are stored below and away from food to prevent potentials for cross-contamination. 
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed cheese on the grill line by the fryers to be out of temperature, 46F, with no time marking. Also, observed cheese on the grill line by the ice machine to be out of temperature, 47F, without time marking. Ensure that PHFs are time marked when they come out of temperature to ensure that they are discarded after 4 hours. The cheese in this situation has an 8 hour time frame due to documentation on the tempering process of the cheese. Manager went through and time marked all products.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed the following: 1) Tomatoes on grill-line by the ice machine to be at 56F and not time marked. Cheese in the same area at 67F and not time marked. 2) Observed tomatoes and cheese on grill-line by drive thru that was out, and not time marked, at 54F and 57F, respectively. 3) Observed burgers on top of burger cooler at 55F with no time marking. Manager time marked all items at this time. See remarks for Time as Control policy.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed burgers in the grill-line burger cooler that were at 49F when probed. The cooler that they were in was noted to not be functioning by the GM at time of spot check. Burgers were pulled and placed in walk-in cooler with time marking. Time as Control would be used on these burgers and they were to be discarded after 4 hours. 
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
750-140b- Observed cooked burger meat in a freezer with other chili ingredients that was labeled for chili, but there was no date marking for the 7 day time frame. Meat was noted to be fully frozen at this time.
Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750.153a - A) Containers of American cheese slices were observed out in the prep area. Management noted cheese is good at ambient temperature for up to 8hrs, with 1hr of that time frame used for tempering the product. Time was not written on any of the containers of cheese slices, including those that were already on the make lines for use. Benefit of doubt was given for cheese and time was marked on all pans. 
Make sure the time is indicated on the pans for cheese to indicate the 8hr time frame for use when product is pulled from coolers. When using time as a control, food shall be marked to indicate the time when it was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Properly label food.
findings.citation_text:
750.153 & 250 - B) Potentially hazardous foods in the top holding area of a front line cooler were observed to have internal temperatures above 41F. Internal temperatures ranged for butter and sour cream packets at 47F-64F dependent upon where the packet was within the pan. Management was advised the cooler being used at this time was not maintaining products at proper temperature. Based on the shift's managers time of set-up the items had already been out for four hours. Items were discarded at this time.
   
Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41F/below while on display and service, unless time control is used. Keep track of the time for foods placed on the cold make lie and use or discard w/in 4hrs.

750-120(a)- C) Burgers and chicken above grill line burger fridge were noted to be at an internal probed temperature of 49F and 45F, respectively. The manager was notified that the raw meat was outside of proper temperature ranges and that time as control would need to be used on the meat. (See General Comments)
Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment:
750.140(a)- Grill line burger cooler did not have a working thermometer noted until the manager brought one over that he said they use for testing it. The external thermometer was not properly working at the time of the inspection. Maintain functioning thermometers in all coolers. 
All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
750-120 - There were lids noted under the dining room counters near the soda service area that were exposed to potential soda syrup and waste water splash. 
All food related items should be protected from potential cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
750-120(a)- A) Bacon was placed in a holding area, but none of the bacon containers had covers. Manager was notified and he immediately placed a baking sheet over the bacon containers to stop debris from falling into the containers. All containers should be protected from debris.  

B) Lettuce within the walk-in cooler was noted to be uncovered. Manager was notified and he stated he would rectify the issue immediately. 
Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510a - Witnessed an employee come into business and wash his hands without using a barrier to turn off the faucet. Employee was beginning his shift and was getting ready to begin handling food. Employee was stopped and educated on proper hand washing technique. Employee rewashed his hands properly. Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:

B) Observed the baffles of the ice machine to have mold accumulation. The ice machine needs to be cleaned and sanitized.
C) Observed dry food splash on the ceiling of the microwave. Microwave was not observed to have been used during inspection. Microwaves need to be properly cleaned and sanitized regularly. 
To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750-800e- The following surfaces were found to be soiled or in disrepair: A) Grill line burger cooler needs cleaned at hinges. B) Scraper container. C) General surfaces around hot holding area. D) Dry storage door and area by drive-thru. E) Upright freezer next to fryers noted to be soiled. F) Bottom of chili meat freezer. G) Shelves within the walk-in cooler noted to have mold accumulation. H) Cabinet next to soda machines in dining room need to be wiped out and cleaned.
Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
750-880- A) Coffee filters were sitting out next to the sink. This posses a risk for possible cross contamination.
B) Single service wrappers on hot holding area were soiled with food debris. They were contained in a proper storage area. Ensure the storage areas are maintained in a clean and sanitary manner.
C) Noted boxes of single-service articles on floor of back storage area. Ensure these boxes are maintained and stored 6 inches off of the ground on a proper surface.
Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment:
750-1130(e)- Observed a mop bucket full of a dirty liquid that had a pudding-like consistency. Asked the on-shift manager about the mop bucket and he said it was dirty water from the night before. He also noted the consistency was from excess grease mopped up off of the floors. Manager was notified that the mop water needed emptied immediately. Employee emptied mop bucket. 
Liquid waste from compacting or cleaning operations shall be disposed of as sewage.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.comment:
750-1130a- Upon arrival for inspection, it was noted that an employee emptied trash into the dumpster and did not close the dumpster after he was finished. Dumpster must be maintained in a manner to prevent pest infestations.
Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
750-1220- A) Observed the back dish area to be soiled throughout the back corner underneath the sink. 
B) Observed the freezer that is within the walk-in cooler to have an accumulation of debris on the floors. 
C) Observed the walk-in freezer with buns to have ice accumulation on the floor.
D) Floor behind single service rack next to mop sink had standing water noted. 
Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
750-1220- A) Observed the wall behind the dish motor, next to the sink, and the caulking for the sink to have mold and grease accumulation.
B) Observed a ceiling tile above the dish area and next to single service items to be in disrepair.
C) Observed fans and back wall of walk-in freezer for buns to have ice accumulation. Ice build up needs to be minimized within this freezer. 
All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning and maintained clean.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
750-1300- Observed a sanitizer bottle sitting next to vegetable oil on a food surface. Attempted to test sanitizer bottle for concentration, but was stopped by the manager. Manager noted the bottle was filled with degreaser and not sanitizer. He was notified that this was improper practice and that the bottle needed to be emptied, cleaned, and filled with sanitizer immediately. Manager rectified the issue at this time.  
Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750.153a - A) Containers of American cheese slices were observed out in the prep area. Management noted cheese is good at ambient temperature for up to 8hrs, with 1hr of that time frame used for tempering the product. Time was not written on any of the containers of cheese slices, including those that were already on the make lines for use. Benefit of doubt was given for cheese and time was marked on all pans. 
Make sure the time is indicated on the pans for cheese to indicate the 8hr time frame for use when product is pulled from coolers. When using time as a control, food shall be marked to indicate the time when it was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Properly label food.
findings.citation_text:
750.153 & 250 - B) Potentially hazardous foods in the top holding area of a make line cooler were observed to have internal temperatures above 41F. Internal temperatures ranged from 45F to 66F, with pans of shredded cheese at 48F and 52F, mayo at 55F, sliced tomatoes at 45F, and butter and sour cream packets at 51F-66F dependent upon where the packet was within the pan. Management was advised the ice bath being used at this time was not maintaining products at proper temperature. Time control will be used for foods in the top holding area of the make line cooler on the grill side of the kitchen until the cooler is repaired and holding proper temperature (see general comments).
   
Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41F/below while on display and service, unless time control is used. Keep track of the time for foods placed on the cold make lie and use or discard w/in 4hrs.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 530f - Employee was observed washing hands without use of proper technique. Hands were rinsed and not lathered/washed for 20 seconds. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with the employee and management. Employee rewashedhis hands with proper technique at request of inspector. Employee also removed a watch from his wrist per the inspector's request.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
Food employees shall not wear jewelry on their arms and hands while preparing food, except for a plain ring such as a wedding band or medical information jewelry.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Employee was observed doing dishes, and a knifed was briefly dunked in sanitizer prior to being placed back in storage rack. Proper sanitizing of equipment for 60 seconds in solution during ware washing was discussed with the employee and management. Knife was placed back in sanitizer to finish properly sanitizing prior to air drying.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4). Equipment and utensils must be submerged in sanitizer solution for at least one minute prior to removing from solution to air dry.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Mold was observed inside the ice machine on the baffle and inner surface of the door. Management had an employee begin wiping down the inner surface of the lid with sanitizer solution during the inspection. Proper cleaning and sanitizing inside the ice machine was discussed with management.  A layer of ice would be removed from inside the machine prior to use after wiping down surfaces.

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris,

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Holder for cup lids at drive thru was observed with buildup along edges where lids rest. Clean and sanitize the lid holders and other storage areas for single service articles as needed to eliminate buildup of debris and protect items from contamination.
 

Single service articles shall be stored, handled and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.

Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.citation_text:

A proper shield was observed in the manager's office. A new bulb needs to be purchased for the freezer. Once new bulb is in place it will be covered with the shield.

Permanently fixed artificial light sources shall be installed to provide, at a distance of 30 inches from the floor at least 10 foot-candles of light in walk-in refrigeration, dry storage areas, and in all other areas. 
All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen areas of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.

750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.

Repair door.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:

Provide test strips to check concentration of sanitizing solutions. 
*note* the lack of test strips contributed to the establishment being unaware that the sanitizer dispenser was not working properly. 
750-830g Chemical test kits for checking sanitizing solutions shall be provided.

Repair dispenser to properly dispense chemical into the mix to make a proper concentration of solution to sanitize equipment and surfaces.

 Properly store and protect food.

Clean this equipment as necessary.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
Observed a donut sitting on the counter at the beginning of inspection.  There should be a designated area for employees to eat. Food was discarded during the inspection.  Use the designated area to eat food on breaks.
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
1.) Observed a leak at the two part sink  2) Observed a leak at the three compartment sink.  3) Observed a leak under the handwashing sink in drive thru area.  Sinks all leak when water is turned on.  Repair the leaks.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed the backdoor of the establishment to be broken.  Replace the self-closer of the door. A follow up will be performed.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1) (REPEAT)  Observed caulk at the men's restrooms to be coming apart from the wall.  Replace the caulk.
2) Observed caulk at the three compartment sink to have black mold accumulation.  Strip and re-caulk this area to make it a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
